newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 13.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - May 13.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

PARIS - Maurice Levy, chairman of French advertising group Publicis, denies there is any conflict between two daughters of the late founder of Publicis, Marcel Bleustein-Blanchet, over one daughter's plan to sell her Publicis holdings. He says, Michele Bleustein-Blanchet, has no timescale for selling all or part of the 20 percent she holds directly or indirectly in Publicis.
DUBAI - Saudi Arabia's billionaire Prince al-Waleed bin Talal says he has bought over three percent of London-based advertising and marketing group Cordiant Plc for 150 million riyals ($40 million).

FRANKFURT - One of Germany's top advertising executives calls for a lifting of the ban on advertising during television news broadcasts, saying it leads to worse and not better news programming. Willi Schalk, chief executive of advertising giant McCann-Erickson's German group, says news programming by private broadcasters suffers from a lack of advertising funding.
LONDON - WPP Group Plc, the advertising and marketing services group, says it has taken a stake in San Francisco-based company HyperParallel which helps firms make use of consumer data.

COPENHAGEN - Danish brewer Carlsberg says it will air interactive television commercial, with a spot for its Tuborg Super Light beer on the country's TV2. The 90-second live spot will give viewers the chance to direct, by telephone, a Tuborg delivery van as it attempts to negotiate a maze.

LONDON- The world's biggest public relations and communications firm, Burson-Marsteller, has completed a worldwide restructuring that has brought pain, but has also paid off, Ferdinand de Bakker, European chief executive says. The restructuring was designed to "shake things up, to prevent us from becoming bureaucratic," he says.
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

TOKYO - Media tycoon Rupert Murdoch's Japanese satellite broadcasting venture appears to have stolen a march on its rivals by recruiting Japanese Fuji Television Network to join Japan Sky Broadcasting Corp (JSkyB), industry experts say.
NEW YORK - Paxson Communications Corp says it has agreed to acquire WBIS+, Channel 31 in New York City, from a partnership of Dow Jones Inc and ITT Corp in a transaction valued at $257.5 million.

PARIS - A new war has broken out between the arch rivals of French television, Canal Plus and Television par Satellite, over pre-purchasing films made by French producers for showing on their channels.
TOKYO - Japan's Toshiba Corp says it will soon launch a compact, home-use personal computer that can be used with a TV screen to run PC software and surf the Internet.

MUNICH - German media conglomerate Bertelsmann AG and the internet services company Lycos Inc of the United States say they have formed a European joint venture. Lycos, a so-called search engine that allows Internet users to locate pages on the World Wide Web, and Bertelsmann plan to offer web directory services in 37 European countries in local language versions.
NEW YORK - General Electric Co's National Broadcasting Co formally unveils its autumn prime time televison lineup with a schedule blanketed by comedy programs.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS, MARKETS & CONSUMER TRENDS

LONDON - British drinks giants Guinness and Grand Metropolitan unveil 23 billion pound ($37 billion) merger aimed at tackling difficult conditions in a fragmented market by creating the world's leading spirits and wine company.

LONDON - Sir Christopher Hogg, chairman of drinks to pub group Allied Domecq, says the company will appeal to regulatory authorities over the planned merger between Grand Metropolitan Plc and Guinness if its in shareholders interests.

BRUSSELS - Belgian brewery group Interbrew says it has signed a distribution deal with Asahi Brewery Ltd, one of Japan's largest breweries, for the distribution of Belle-Vue Kriek beer. A second deal has been clinched with Konishi Brewing Co. Ltd. for the distribution of the Hoegaarden range of beers.
MEXICO CITY - In the first quarter of 1997, Mexican beer exports totalled $94.1 million, up 17.8 percent over the same period a year earlier, the National Statistics Institute says.

BEIJING - Hong Kong watches, coins and refrigerator magnets are just some of the baubles that China's entrepreneurs have cooked up to tap into a wave of patriotic sentiment over Beijing's resumption of sovereignty over the territory at midnight on June 30.
BREMEN, Germany - German coffee lovers will have to pay more as retail prices of roasted coffee rise to 12 marks ($7.03) per 500-gram packet from 10 marks, Kraft Jacobs Suchard says.

FRANKFURT - The European car market is set for a choppy but certain recovery over the next three years, moving toward unit sales levels not seen since the early part of this decade, industry analysts say.

HONG KONG - Swire Pacific Ltd says its newly-formed automotive subsidiary, Taikoo Motors Ltd, will distribute Volvo cars in Hong Kong and southern and central China. Swire Pacific has been a Volvo distributor in Taiwan since 1977 and in northern and eastern China since 1993.
